claims.statement: Published rehabilitation checks and message specifications make a deterministic local preflight technically plausible and show recurring rule-version work.
The 2,768-provider 2023 population is large enough for discovery but does not validate a 250-350 customer outcome or a narrow independent-provider segment.
Incumbent Polish HIS products already automate rehabilitation cycles and NFZ settlement, so the product must demonstrate incremental detection rather than duplicate core workflow.
On-premise or pseudonymized processing can reduce exposure but does not by itself remove GDPR risk assessment, security, contracting, and possible DPIA duties.
The reviewed evidence does not quantify preventable rejection value, incremental errors beyond incumbents, connector rights, willingness to pay, sales cost, support burden, or renewal.

contrary_evidence: mMedica and KS-SOMED already provide directly overlapping rehabilitation and NFZ settlement functions.
Public specifications reduce proprietary rule advantage.
Privacy and security obligations remain even with local-first deployment.
Provider population is not evidence of rejection pain or purchasing intent.
